lessons.title: Incoming Coil Inspection & Traceability
lessons.description: Receiving, Hard Stamping & Heat Lineage Verification

content.text:
A 28-metric-ton hot-rolled steel coil arrives on the heavy transport saddle at Bay 1. Before the overhead gantry crane mounts it onto the decoiler car, the operator must verify the physical heat stamp against the mill test certificate (MTR) to prevent mixed-steel heats in high-pressure gas pipeline orders.

Station 1 Receiving Checklist

Scan barcode tag and compare against SAP/MES production schedule.

Locate the low-stress hard stamp on the strip outer wrap and confirm Heat Number, Coil ID, and Steel Grade (e.g., API 5L X70M).

Perform 3-point ultrasonic thickness measurement: operator side edge, centerline, and drive side edge.

Inspect coil edges for physical transit damage, gouges, or telescoping exceeding 30 mm.

Traceability begins before the steel is cut. When in doubt on heat lineage, stop and tag.

quiz.question: You scan an incoming coil tag marked Heat #8410, but the permanent hard stamp pressed into the coil edge clearly reads Heat #8419. What is your correct first action?
quiz.context: The crane operator is waiting to load the coil on the entry saddle to keep the line moving.

options.text: Proceed with uncoiling because the numbers only differ by the last single digit.
options.explanation: Incorrect. In certified pipeline manufacturing, a single digit difference represents an entirely different metallurgical batch. Mixing heats without authorization invalidates customer certifications.

options.text: Immediately halt loading, affix a physical Yellow Hold tag, and notify Quality Control.
options.explanation: Correct! Material traceability in API 5L manufacturing is absolute. Any conflict between digital paperwork and physical steel stamps mandates an immediate Hold and quality escalation before the coil enters processing.

options.text: Take a permanent marker and rewrite the tag number over the steel stamp.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Tampering with or altering hard-stamped numbers is a severe compliance violation and constitutes falsification of quality records.

options.text: Uncoil the first 5 meters to see if the inner stamp matches the tag.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Loading and uncoiling discrepant material risks contaminating downstream cutters and welders. Verification must occur prior to mounting.

quiz.standardReference: API 5L Section 10.2 / Welspun QAP Traceability Clause 4.1

content.text:
The steel coil unwinds through the heavy hydraulic peeler knife into the 9-roll flattener. To eliminate residual curvature from coiling, alternating hydraulic rolls level the steel strip flat. High-speed carbide milling cutters then shave both edges simultaneously into precision double-V bevels.

Leveler & Milling Station Checks

Inspect top and bottom leveler roll surfaces for foreign metal particles or gouges.

Verify hydraulic leveler pressure is within target setpoint (175 - 195 bar).

Check edge milling carbide indexable inserts every 400 meters for chipping or excessive wear.

Measure milled bevel geometry using the calibrated protractor gauge: 30° (+2°/-0°) and 1.5 mm root face.

Precise edge milling geometry guarantees sound root fusion. Monitor insert wear and root land constantly.

quiz.question: During mid-shift inspection, your bevel gauge shows the drive-side root face has widened to 3.2 mm (target: 1.5 mm). What is the primary welding risk if this strip continues into the forming head?
quiz.context: The milling machine vibration has slightly shifted the vertical cutter cartridge.

options.text: The pipe will suffer Lack of Penetration (LOP) in the root seam.
options.explanation: Correct! When the root face is twice as thick as specified (3.2 mm vs 1.5 mm), the heat from the submerged arc welding electrodes cannot completely fuse through the root thickness, leaving an unfused seam gap (Lack of Penetration).

options.text: The pipe will immediately become oval during hydrostatic testing.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Ovality is governed by roll forming geometry and cold expanding, not root face thickness.

options.text: The outer pipe coating will crack during cooling.
options.explanation: Incorrect. External 3LPE coating occurs much later downstream after pipe fabrication and testing.

options.text: The strip will slip off the drive roller conveyor.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Edge bevel geometry does not control strip mechanical conveyor traction.

quiz.standardReference: WPS-HSAW-01 / API 5L Appendix D Welding Procedures

lessons.title: Helical Forming & Three-Roll Geometry
lessons.description: Forming Angle Kinematics & Dynamic Continuous Curvature

content.text:
The flat, milled strip enters the forming head at a carefully calibrated angle α. Three heavy hydraulic bending rolls curve the strip continuously into a hollow spiral cylinder. As the strip curls around, its trailing edge meets the leading edge of the previously formed spiral loop with sub-millimeter precision.

Forming Head Console Operation

Verify forming angle setting on the digital resolver readout matches the setup sheet for the scheduled pipe diameter.

Observe laser seam tracker camera monitor: ensure seam gap remains between 0.6 mm and 1.2 mm.

Inspect edge offset ("high-low") across the meeting strip edges; must not exceed 1.0 mm.

Check hydraulic roll pressure balance across the primary bending roll, exit roll, and bottom guide support.

Forming angle and edge gap determine weld geometry. Never let strip edges overlap before the welding torch.

quiz.question: While observing the laser seam tracker at 48-inch pipe production, you notice the gap is pinching shut (0.0 mm) and strip edges are beginning to climb over each other. Which corrective action should the operator take?
quiz.context: A slight strip camber in the incoming coil is pushing the strip harder against the inner guide.

options.text: Increase welding arc amperage to melt the overlapped steel away.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Welding over overlapped edges creates gross mechanical misalignment, severe weld defects, and potential torch burnouts.

options.text: Fine-tune the exit guide roll / adjust side guide position to restore the proper 0.6–1.2 mm seam gap.
options.explanation: Correct! Compensating for incoming coil camber requires micro-adjustment of the side guide roll and exit roll position, relieving mechanical edge overlap and restoring the nominal seam gap before welding.

options.text: Speed up the line feed drive to break through the pinch point.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Accelerating into edge overlap can jam the forming head, fracture roll bearings, or cause emergency line trip.

options.text: Shut off the laser seam tracker so alarms stop sounding.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Disabling safety and tracking sensors violates operating procedures and leads to uncontrolled product defects.

quiz.standardReference: Standard Operating Procedure SOP-FORM-03: Camber & Gap Control

lessons.title: Submerged Arc Welding (SAW)
lessons.description: Dual-Sided Tandem Wire SAW Under Granular Flux Blanket

content.text:
Immediately after temporary continuous gas-metal arc tacking, the formed helical seam is welded permanently using Submerged Arc Welding (SAW). The process occurs in two passes: first on the inside of the pipe (ID pass) and then on the outside (OD pass), with high-amperage wire electrodes buried deep beneath a blanket of protective granular flux.

SAW Welding Console Station

Verify preheat temperature on thick-wall strip is above minimum threshold (> 80°C).

Check flux delivery hopper level and ensure vacuum suction returns unfused flux continuously.

Monitor welding electrical parameters on console: Lead Wire (DC+) 850A / 34V; Trail Wire (AC) 750A / 38V.

Verify flux is clean, dry, and baked per procedure (moisture content < 0.1%).

Dry flux and stable electrical parameters prevent porosity. Guard against moisture at all times.

quiz.question: A flux hopper heating element fails, allowing cold, ambient humid flux to enter the welding zone. What critical weld defect is most likely to develop?
quiz.context: Atmospheric humidity is 85% during monsoon season at the plant.

options.text: Excessive pipe ovality.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Ovality is governed by roll forming geometry, not weld flux chemistry.

options.text: Hydrogen-induced cold cracking and wormhole porosity in the weld bead.
options.explanation: Correct! Moisture in SAW flux dissociates at arc temperatures into atomic hydrogen and oxygen. Hydrogen dissolves into the molten weld pool and causes porosity, as well as delayed cold cracking (Hydrogen-Induced Cracking - HIC) as the weld cools under restraint.

options.text: Premature dulling of the edge milling cutters.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Edge milling occurs upstream before the strip enters the welding station.

options.text: Loss of hydraulic pump pressure in the uncoiler.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Welding flux moisture has no interaction with hydraulic fluid systems.

quiz.standardReference: WPS-HSAW-01 Section 6: Flux Storage, Baking and Handling

lessons.title: Quality Testing: Hydrostatic & NDT
lessons.description: 100% Phased-Array Ultrasonic Testing & Proof Pressure Hydrotesting

content.text:
After the continuous pipe is cut into 12-meter lengths by the automated flying plasma saw, each individual pipe joint undergoes rigorous non-destructive evaluation. First, an automated multi-probe Ultrasonic Testing (UT) gantry scans the entire spiral weld seam. Then the pipe is clamped in the hydrostatic tester and pumped with high-pressure water to stress the steel to 90% of its yield limit.

Hydrostatic & UT Inspection Operations

Verify all air is purged through air bleed valves before pressure ramp-up.

Confirm target test pressure setpoint on digital chart recorder (e.g. 145 bar / 2100 PSI).

Hold test pressure for mandatory duration (minimum 10.0 seconds per API 5L).

Watch pressure decay curve: pressure drop must be 0.0 bar during the hold window.

Check automated UT console for green pass status on weld seam and heat-affected zone (HAZ).

Hydrostatic pressure testing proves integrity under real stress. Never accept a pressure drop.

quiz.question: During the 10-second hydrostatic test hold at 145 bar, the digital chart recorder shows pressure dropping steadily from 145 bar down to 132 bar. No water is spraying from the end gaskets. What does this indicate?
quiz.context: The pipe joint is pressurized with filtered water inside the guarded test bay.

options.text: The test passes because pressure stayed above 130 bar.
options.explanation: Incorrect. API 5L mandates zero pressure drop during the hold period. Any drop indicates loss of containment.

options.text: The water was too cold, which caused normal thermal contraction.
options.explanation: Incorrect. A 13-bar pressure drop in 10 seconds cannot be attributed to ambient thermal contraction in heavy industrial pipe bodies.

options.text: A pressure-containing leak or micro-fissure is present; the pipe fails the test and must be quarantined.
options.explanation: Correct! Any measurable pressure drop during the mandatory hold duration proves that pressurized water is escaping through a through-weld flaw, pinhole, or structural defect. The pipe fails proof testing and must be quarantined for NDT root-cause investigation.

options.text: The operator should immediately repressurize to 160 bar to seal the leak.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Never over-pressurize a leaking pipe under test; doing so risks catastrophic burst and violates certified test procedures.

quiz.standardReference: API 5L Section 10.2.6 / Mill Test Procedure TP-HYDRO-01

lessons.title: Release & Dispatch: Coating & Traceability Stencil
lessons.description: Precision End Beveling, 3LPE External Coating & Final Stenciling

content.text:
Having passed all mechanical and non-destructive quality gates, the pipe joint enters the finishing bay. Machine tools face and bevel the pipe ends to precise angles for pipeline field welding. The outer surface receives a high-performance 3-Layer Polyethylene (3LPE) anti-corrosion coating, followed by automated computer-controlled white stencil marking of full pedigree data.

Finishing & Dispatch Checklist

Inspect end bevel angle (30° with 1.6 mm root face) using calibrated bevel protractor.

Run the high-voltage holiday detector spark brush (25 kV) over 100% of the coated pipe body; ensure zero spark alarms.

Verify dry film thickness (DFT) of 3LPE coating exceeds minimum contract specification (> 2.8 mm).

Check stenciled text on pipe body and inside diameter end: verify Heat Number, Pipe Serial Number, Steel Grade, and Welspun Monogram.

The finished pipe carries the Welspun name. 100% coating integrity and clear stenciling ensure 50 years of safe service.

quiz.question: While testing the coated pipe body with the 25 kV holiday spark detector, a loud buzzer sounds and an electric blue spark jumps from the brush to the pipe metal at the 7-meter mark. What is the required disposition?
quiz.context: The pipe is on the final inspection roller bed prior to railcar loading.

options.text: Wipe the area with a wet cloth to silence the alarm and approve the pipe.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Silencing alarms without investigation conceals coating defects that cause premature pipeline corrosion in field service.

options.text: Paint over the spot with standard industrial spray paint.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Spray paint does not meet 3LPE dielectric insulation or moisture barrier requirements.

options.text: Mark the pinhole (holiday), perform an approved heat-shrink patch repair per procedure, and re-test with the spark detector.
options.explanation: Correct! The spark detector detects a microscopic pinhole or void through the polyethylene layer down to the bare steel. Per ISO 21809-1, the defect must be marked, abraded, repaired with an approved cross-linked polyolefin repair patch, and 100% spark re-tested before release.

options.text: Ship the pipe as-is because the customer will apply field tape anyway.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Factory-applied coatings must meet zero-holiday acceptance prior to delivery.

quiz.standardReference: ISO 21809-1 Clause 10.3 Holiday Testing / Coating QAP-3LPE-01

title: Shop Floor Safety Essentials
description: Master the critical plant safety principles required across heavy manufacturing: full personal protective equipment (PPE), heavy crane suspended load hazards, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) energy isolation, and proactive incident reporting.

modules.title: Shop Floor Safety Essentials
modules.description: Master the critical plant safety principles required across heavy manufacturing: full personal protective equipment (PPE), heavy crane suspended load hazards, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) energy isolation, and proactive incident reporting.

content.text:
Entering the high-bay manufacturing area requires immediate transition into full industrial PPE. Massive 30-ton steel coils, high-temperature plasma cutters, and heavy overhead cranes operate 24 hours a day. Marked yellow floor pathways protect pedestrians from automated transfer buggies and heavy machinery.

Turnstile PPE Verification Checklist

Hard hat securely fastened with 4-point ratchet suspension (ensure no cracks or stickers hiding damage).

Safety glasses with side shields certified to ANSI Z87.1 (over-glasses for prescription wearers).

Class 2 High-Visibility reflective safety vest zipped shut over clothing.

Steel-toe safety boots with integrated metatarsal guard (ASTM F2413 approved).

Hearing protection (earplugs or earmuffs) with NRR rating > 28 dB.

Safety gear is non-negotiable. Stop-Work Authority empowers every employee to protect anyone at risk.

quiz.question: You see a contractor walking through the active pipe transfer bay without safety glasses while a welder is grinding weld spatter 5 meters away. What should you do?
quiz.context: You are walking along the designated yellow walkway toward your machine station.

options.text: Ignore the contractor because they are not part of your immediate work crew.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Safety responsibility belongs to everyone. Flying debris does not distinguish between contractors and full-time employees.

options.text: Exercise your Stop-Work Authority, politely stop the contractor, and guide them to the safety glasses dispenser station.
options.explanation: Correct! Every employee at Welspun possesses absolute Stop-Work Authority. Intervening immediately prevents irreversible eye injury from flying metallic sparks and grinding dust.

options.text: Wait until the end of your shift to submit a note to HR.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Delayed reporting does nothing to protect the worker from immediate physical danger happening right now.

options.text: Shout at the contractor across the bay while continuing to walk.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Shouting across loud machinery can startle personnel near moving equipment. Approach safely and address the hazard constructively.

quiz.standardReference: Welspun Plant Safety Policy: Stop-Work Authority Charter

lessons.title: Hazard Identification, Suspended Loads & Pinch Points
lessons.description: Line of Fire Awareness & Stored Mechanical Energy

content.text:
Heavy manufacturing environments contain significant kinetic and stored mechanical energy. High-bay overhead cranes move 30-ton coils through the air, while tightly coiled steel strips store massive spring-like tension. Operators must stay out of the "Line of Fire" at all times.

Suspended Load & Coil Band Protocol

Listen for crane warning siren/strobe and immediately look up to locate the crane position.

Never stand, walk, or position any body part beneath a suspended load or crane hook.

Maintain a minimum clearance cone: distance equal to load height plus 3 meters.

When cutting coil packaging bands, use pneumatic band cutters with safety hold-down arms deployed.

Stand to the side outside the radial recoil arc when shearing the final steel retention band.

Never position yourself beneath a suspended load. Respect stored energy and stay out of the Line of Fire.

quiz.question: An overhead crane is transporting a 25-ton coil toward the uncoiler. The crane travel buzzer is sounding, and the load path passes directly over your workbench. What is your immediate action?
quiz.context: You are preparing an ultrasonic calibration block on your workbench.

options.text: Stay at your workbench and keep your head down until the crane passes.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Remaining under a suspended load places you in the direct Line of Fire in the event of rigging failure or mechanical brake slip.

options.text: Step back immediately out of the crane travel path to a designated safe zone until the load has fully passed.
options.explanation: Correct! You must never remain under a suspended load. Immediately clear the travel corridor and wait until the load has moved past and lowered into its saddle.

options.text: Wave at the crane operator to tell them you are working below.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Crane operators high in the cab have limited visibility angles and cannot react in time if mechanical rigging slips.

options.text: Run quickly directly underneath the moving coil to beat it to the other side.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Running under a moving heavy load drastically increases the risk of tripping and fatal crush injury.

quiz.standardReference: Welspun High-Bay Crane Safety Standard CS-01: Line of Fire

lessons.title: Safe Equipment Operation & Lockout/Tagout (LOTO)
lessons.description: Zero-Energy State Verification & Hazardous Energy Isolation

content.text:
A maintenance technician needs to clean weld spatter and replace the contact nozzle inside the automatic submerged arc welding head carriage. Even though the operator console switch is set to "Stop", high-voltage electrical, 200-bar hydraulic, and 8-bar pneumatic lines remain connected to the machine.

The 6-Step LOTO Procedure

1. Notify affected operators that the machine is entering lockout.

2. Shut down equipment using normal stopping sequence.

3. Isolate all energy sources: turn main electrical breaker to OFF, close hydraulic isolating valve, close pneumatic valve.

4. Apply personal red padlock and danger tag to the lockout hasp (one person, one lock, one key).

5. Dissipate stored energy: bleed hydraulic accumulator pressure to 0 bar, drain air receivers, apply mechanical safety wedges.

6. Verify Zero Energy State: push the machine start button to confirm it does not turn on, then return switch to OFF.

One person, one lock, one key. Never trust control switches for body protection.

quiz.question: You need 30 seconds to wipe dust off an optical sensor located between two hydraulic forming rolls. Can you just press the Emergency Stop button on the pendant instead of performing full LOTO?
quiz.context: The line is running on schedule and you want to be quick.

options.text: Yes, because 30 seconds is too short to justify full lockout.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Duration does not alter the hazard. A machine can crush or sever a limb in less than 0.2 seconds.

options.text: Yes, as long as another operator promises to stand next to the console.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Human communication and promises fail. Another person cannot physically stop a hydraulic valve from drifting or malfunctioning.

options.text: No. An E-stop is a control device, not energy isolation. Full LOTO and zero-energy verification are mandatory before placing hands in pinch points.
options.explanation: Correct! E-stops, light curtains, and safety doors are control circuits that can short-circuit or fail. Any body entry into machinery pinch points mandates complete physical energy isolation, padlock application, and zero-energy verification.

options.text: Yes, provided the hydraulic motor is turned off.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Even if the pump is off, hydraulic accumulators hold high residual pressure that can cause roll movement until bled.

quiz.standardReference: OSHA 1910.147 / Welspun Life-Saving Rule #2: Energy Isolation

content.text:
While walking past the hydrostatic tester transfer conveyor, an operator notices a high-pressure hydraulic flex hose weeping fluid onto the concrete floor near an electrical conduit. Nobody has slipped or been hurt yet.

Near-Miss Action Steps

1. Make the area safe immediately: place a caution cone, barricade, or spill absorbent pad.

2. Notify the area supervisor verbally.

3. Log the near-miss on the digital safety kiosk or mobile app within the same shift.

4. Confirm the maintenance work order is assigned and tracked to completion.

Every near-miss is a lesson before an injury. Report hazards immediately to protect your team.

quiz.question: You find an oily slick on the walkway near the pipe flattener. Nobody has fallen. What is the proper procedure?
quiz.context: You are halfway through your shift and have production targets to meet.

options.text: Walk around it; maintenance will probably see it during their weekly sweep.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Leaving a known hazard unaddressed invites the next passing employee to slip, fall, and sustain injury.

options.text: Throw a piece of cardboard over the oil so nobody sees it.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Cardboard absorbs oil and becomes an even more dangerous, hidden slip hazard.

options.text: Place a hazard cone, contain the oil with absorbent pads, and file a Near-Miss report so the leak gets repaired.
options.explanation: Correct! Immediate containment protects your coworkers, and filing the near-miss report ensures the root mechanical oil leak is repaired by maintenance before someone gets hurt.

options.text: Only report it if someone actually falls and needs medical attention.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Waiting for an actual injury before reporting defeats the entire purpose of proactive safety culture.

quiz.standardReference: Welspun Incident Reporting & Near-Miss Guideline SAF-04

description: Learn the foundations of certified manufacturing quality: quality gate checkpoints, weld defect classification, heat number traceability, and non-conformance quarantine decisions.

lessons.title: Inspection Checkpoints & Sampling Intervals
lessons.description: Quality Gates, Gauge Calibration & Frequency Control

content.text:
In API 5L linepipe production, quality is verified at predetermined inspection gates: incoming raw coil, continuous strip milling, helical welding, hydrostatic proof testing, ultrasonic testing, and final release. Every measuring tool must carry a valid calibration sticker.

Shift Start Quality Tool Check

Inspect calibration sticker on calipers, micrometers, and ultrasonic thickness gauges: verify expiration date has not passed.

Perform zero-point check on micrometers against calibrated gauge blocks.

Verify inspection log sheets are loaded with the correct client specification and tolerance limits.

Record physical measurements at mandated intervals: measure wall thickness at 4 quadrants on every 10th pipe.

Never measure with an expired tool. Calibration validity is the foundation of certified quality.

quiz.question: Your digital micrometer has a calibration sticker that expired yesterday, but it reads zero when closed and looks clean. Can you use it for the morning inspection run?
quiz.context: The tool crib is at the far end of the plant building.

options.text: Yes, as long as it reads zero when closed.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Reading zero does not verify linearity, accuracy across the measurement range, or anvil parallelism.

options.text: No. Using an expired tool invalidates quality certifications; you must replace it immediately with a calibrated tool from the tool crib.
options.explanation: Correct! Under API Spec Q1 and ISO 9001, any measurement taken with an instrument whose calibration interval has expired is legally invalid. If an audit reveals expired tools were used, every pipe measured with that tool can be rejected by the customer.

options.text: Yes, but apply a manual 5% correction factor to your notes.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Operators cannot invent arbitrary correction factors. All instruments must have documented calibration traceability.

options.text: Yes, but only for the first two pipes of the shift.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Quality standards apply to every pipe without exception.

quiz.standardReference: API Spec Q1 Section 5.8: Control of Testing and Measuring Equipment

lessons.title: Defect Awareness & Classification
lessons.description: Weld & Base Metal Defects: Porosity, Undercut & LOP

content.text:
Quality inspectors must recognize and classify weld and metal imperfections: undercut, porosity clusters, lack of penetration (LOP), lack of fusion, slag inclusions, and base metal laminations. Critical planar defects have zero tolerance in high-pressure oil and gas pipelines.

Weld Inspection & Visual Identification

Inspect weld bead crown for uniform width and smooth transition into base metal.

Check for undercut: grooves along the edge of the weld bead toe must not exceed 0.5 mm in depth.

Verify absence of surface porosity, pinholes, or crater cracks.

Inspect base metal adjacent to weld for arc strikes or heavy mechanical gouges.

Smooth weld transitions prevent fatigue failure. Sharp notches and cracks are strictly unacceptable.

quiz.question: During visual inspection of the outer weld cap, you detect a sharp continuous groove (undercut) along the weld toe measuring 1.2 mm deep over a length of 150 mm. How do you classify this?
quiz.context: API 5L specifies maximum undercut depth of 0.5 mm for continuous defects.

options.text: Acceptable cosmetic imperfection that does not require action.
options.explanation: Incorrect. A 1.2 mm deep undercut is more than double the maximum allowable limit of 0.5 mm.

options.text: Minor flaw that will be concealed by the external 3LPE coating.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Concealing a structural notch under coating creates a dangerous hidden failure point when the pipe is pressurized in the field.

options.text: Critical rejectable defect exceeding API 5L limits; mark the pipe and initiate an approved weld repair procedure.
options.explanation: Correct! Undercut deeper than 0.5 mm creates a severe stress riser that can trigger fatigue cracking under operating pipeline pressures. It exceeds acceptance criteria and requires marking, mechanical grinding/gouging, re-welding per approved procedure, and 100% NDT re-inspection.

options.text: Normal variation that will smooth out during hydrostatic testing.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Hydrostatic testing stresses the pipe; it does not heal or smooth out sharp geometric weld defects.

quiz.standardReference: API Spec 5L Section 9.10 / Defect Catalogue QC-DEF-02

lessons.title: Traceability & Heat Number Lineage
lessons.description: From Ladle Chemical Heat to Final Pipe Serial Number

content.text:
Every single pipe manufactured carries an unbroken lineage tracing back to the original steel ladle heat, chemical composition, coil roll date, welding machine operator, and test charts. If a pipe in a transcontinental pipeline needs verification 30 years from now, its pedigree must be instantly retrievable.

Traceability Verification Steps

Verify internal pipe end low-stress hard stamp matches the physical traveler card before hydro testing.

Ensure computerized pipe stenciler applies clean, legible white text on pipe outer diameter.

Scan pipe barcode at each transfer station to record electronic production tracking.

If stencil is smeared or unreadable, halt pipe transfer and apply permanent manual paint stencil.

Hard stamps and digital lineage protect traceability. Never guess a serial number.

quiz.question: A pipe arrives at final inspection with its external stencil smeared by cooling water, and the paper barcode label is torn off. How should you verify the pipe identity?
quiz.context: Two identical-looking pipes are sitting side-by-side on the inspection rack.

options.text: Guess the serial number based on the previous pipe in the rack sequence (+1).
options.explanation: Incorrect. Never guess serial numbers. If the sequence skipped a pipe due to testing delays, guessing assigns the wrong metallurgical pedigree.

options.text: Locate the permanent low-stress hard stamp inside the pipe end, verify it against the line tracking MES system, and re-stencil.
options.explanation: Correct! The permanent low-stress hard stamp applied inside the pipe end prior to hydrostatic testing is the authoritative physical source of truth. Verifying this hard stamp against the digital MES traveler restores verified traceability.

options.text: Assign a brand-new number from the end of the batch to keep the conveyor moving.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Assigning arbitrary new serial numbers severs the link to the actual steel heat and hydrostatic test certificate.

options.text: Ship the pipe without a stencil and let the customer identify it on site.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Unmarked pipes cannot be accepted by clients and will be rejected at destination ports.

quiz.standardReference: Welspun Traceability Standard SOP-TRAC-02 / API 5L Clause 11

content.text:
When an automated ultrasonic inspection flags an internal weld flaw or hydro test records an anomalous pressure drop, production must instantly stop for that pipe. The pipe is flagged, diverter arms push it into the designated physical quarantine bay, and red HOLD tags are locked in place until formal disposition.

Quarantine Action Protocol

1. Immediately trigger the reject diverter kicker to route pipe into the quarantine holding rack.

2. Affix prominent red "REJECTED / HOLD - DO NOT MOVE" tags to both ends of the pipe.

3. Log the pipe serial number and defect description into the electronic Non-Conformance Report (NCR) system.

4. Confirm red quarantine status lights illuminate above the quarantine rack.

Quality hold is absolute. Only authorized QA personnel can release quarantined material.

quiz.question: A production shift supervisor tells you to remove a red Quarantine tag from a pipe with a minor UT flaw so it can be loaded onto an urgent transport truck to meet the shift quota. What should you do?
quiz.context: The truck driver is waiting at the dispatch bay.

options.text: Remove the tag immediately because the shift supervisor is in charge of production operations.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Production hierarchy cannot overrule quality quarantine. Unauthorized release of quarantined goods is a severe compliance violation.

options.text: Maintain the quarantine, refuse to remove the tag, and immediately escalate the situation to the Quality Assurance Manager.
options.explanation: Correct! Quality quarantine holds are absolute and legally protected. Under API Spec Q1, only authorized Quality Assurance personnel can approve NCR dispositions and release quarantined product. Production schedules never override quality integrity.

options.text: Take the tag off but write a private warning note to the truck driver.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Warning the driver does not fix or verify the defective pipeline weld.

options.text: Hide the pipe in the back of the yard until next week.
options.explanation: Incorrect. Hiding quarantined material prevents formal MRB investigation and repair.

quiz.standardReference: API Spec Q1 Section 5.8 / Welspun Quality Governance Charter

modules.title: coating application External & Internal
modules.description: One pipe, from the receiving bay to the dispatch yard. Sixteen stops, outside coating first, then the inside. At each stop you read it in short parts, look at the real equipment, and make the call an inspector makes.

lessons.title: Why a pipe needs a coat

content.text:
Pipe #W-0417 is bare steel. Buried in soil and water, steel rusts. The coating has one job: keep every corrosive element away from the steel. Everything you will see on this line, from the first wash to the last stencil, exists to make that coat hold.

At your station

Your station either protects the next one or damages it. A coating can only stick to steel that is clean and rough, and it only protects if it is unbroken. That is why surface preparation and testing get as much attention as the coating itself.

Coating families: 3LPE/3LPP, FBE/DFBE, CWC

Test of failure: soil or water touching steel

Backstop: cathodic protection (CP)

A coating is failed if any soil or water makes contact with the pipe steel.

quiz.question: Over a pipeline’s life, some coating damage is found and the CP system is working fully. What does the deck say about this situation?
quiz.context: Pipe #W-0417 is bare steel. Buried in soil and water, steel rusts. The coating has one job: keep every corrosive element away from the steel. Everything you will see on this line, from the first wash to the last stencil, exists to make that coat hold.

The pipe is checked at receiving inspection, then rolls into a high pressure hot water wash. The wash takes off what blasting would otherwise have to fight: loose dust, mud, soluble salts and chlorides. An air knife wipes the water off before the pipe moves on.

At your station

Both flow charts open with receiving inspection, then water wash, which is marked optional (*). Optional means the project specification decides, so check the order before you assume the step is on or off. The same chart shows the NTC re-process loop returning here.

Spray pressure: up to 100 bar

Water temperature: up to 70 °C (if required)

Removes: dust, mud, soluble salts, chlorides

Drying: compressed-air knife

Optional on the chart means “as the project specification requires”, not “skip when busy”.

quiz.question: Looking at the two flow charts, which early station is marked optional on BOTH the 3LPE/3LPP chart and the FBE/DFBE chart?
quiz.context: The pipe is checked at receiving inspection, then rolls into a high pressure hot water wash. The wash takes off what blasting would otherwise have to fight: loose dust, mud, soluble salts and chlorides. An air knife wipes the water off before the pipe moves on.

options.text: Receiving inspection
options.explanation: Water wash carries the asterisk on both charts. Preheating is starred only on the 3LPE/3LPP chart; on the FBE/DFBE chart it is a standard station. The footnote on both says optional stations apply as per project specification requirements.

The pipe enters a gas oven that sits right before the blast machines. Seven radiation burners warm the steel so any wetness is gone before abrasive hits it. Pyrometers watch the temperature all the time.

At your station

Check the pyrometer display at the oven. The steel is raised up to 85 °C, using LPG or natural gas as fuel. The point is a surface free from moisture, not a hot pipe for its own sake.

Burners: 7 × 500 kW

Throughput: 125 MT/hr

Steel temperature: up to 85 °C

Fuel: LPG or natural gas

Monitoring: radiation pyrometers

The oven’s job is to remove wetness before blast cleaning.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of the gas oven before the blast machines?
quiz.context: The pipe enters a gas oven that sits right before the blast machines. Seven radiation burners warm the steel so any wetness is gone before abrasive hits it. Pyrometers watch the temperature all the time.

options.text: To cure the epoxy
options.explanation: The deck states the oven removes any wetness and makes the surface free from moisture before blast cleaning. The 250 °C figure belongs to the induction heater much later in the line.

options.text: To remove wetness so the surface is free from moisture before blast cleaning

Pipe #W-0417 enters the blast machines. Steel grit hurled at 80 metres a second strips away contamination and leaves the surface rough, so the coating has something to grip. It happens in two stages, with two blast wheels in each.

At your station

Two things matter at this station: how clean (Sa2½ to Sa3) and how rough (anchor pattern 50 to 110 microns). The grit is screened all the time and fine dust is pulled out by bag-house collectors, so the pipe and the abrasive stay dust-free.

Cleanliness: Sa2½ to Sa3 (ISO 8501-1)

Anchor pattern: 50 to 110 µm

Stages: 2 sets, 2 wheels each

Throw velocity: 80 m/s

Capacity: 600 m²/hr each, over 800 combined

Abrasive: steel grit GP18/25/40 or shot S280/S330

Cleanliness Sa2½ to Sa3 and anchor pattern 50 to 110 µm. The next station measures both.

quiz.question: Which pair describes what external blasting must deliver, according to the deck?
quiz.context: Pipe #W-0417 enters the blast machines. Steel grit hurled at 80 metres a second strips away contamination and leaves the surface rough, so the coating has something to grip. It happens in two stages, with two blast wheels in each.

options.text: Sa1 to Sa2 and 10 to 50 µm
options.explanation: The deck states Sa2½ to Sa3 against ISO 8501-1 and an anchor pattern of 50 to 110 microns. The next station inspects exactly these two things.

options.text: Sa2½ to Sa3 and 50 to 110 µm
options.explanation: The deck states Sa2½ to Sa3 against ISO 8501-1 and an anchor pattern of 50 to 110 microns. The next station inspects exactly these two things.

options.text: Sa3 only and 200 µm
options.explanation: The deck states Sa2½ to Sa3 against ISO 8501-1 and an anchor pattern of 50 to 110 microns. The next station inspects exactly these two things.

content.text:
This is where the pipe can be stopped. An inspector compares it with the rust-grade book, measures its roughness, checks for salt and dust, and looks for steel or surface defects. OK goes to the coating line. NOT OK takes the NTC re-process route back to receiving inspection.

At your station

Five checks, all must pass: visual cleanliness (Sa2½ to Sa3 against ISO 8501-1 and SSPC-VIS 1 photographs), anchor profile with the digital roughness gauge, salt contamination with the meter, dust degree per ISO 8502-3, and other surface defects.

Cleanliness: Sa2½ to Sa3, visual

Anchor profile: 50 to 110 µm

Salt: measured with meter

Dust: ISO 8502-3 (1 to 5 chart)

NOT OK: NTC re-process

NOT OK is not scrap. It is the re-process route, and the pipe runs surface preparation again.

quiz.question: A blasted pipe passes the visual cleanliness check and the roughness reading. Is the surface inspection finished?
quiz.context: This is where the pipe can be stopped. An inspector compares it with the rust-grade book, measures its roughness, checks for salt and dust, and looks for steel or surface defects. OK goes to the coating line. NOT OK takes the NTC re-process route back to receiving inspection.

options.text: Yes, those two are all that matter
options.explanation: The deck lists five parts to the inspection of surface preparation: cleanliness, anchor profile, salt contamination, degree of dust per ISO 8502-3, and other steel and surface defects. A pipe goes to the coating line only when it clears them all.

options.text: No. Salt contamination, dust degree and any other steel or surface defects are also part of the inspection
options.explanation: The deck lists five parts to the inspection of surface preparation: cleanliness, anchor profile, salt contamination, degree of dust per ISO 8502-3, and other steel and surface defects. A pipe goes to the coating line only when it clears them all.

options.text: Only for FBE pipes

lessons.title: Acid wash and the rinse
lessons.description: PHOSPHORIC ACID AND HIGH PRESSURE WATER WASH

content.text:
After the blast gate and a first induction pre heat, the pipe meets a phosphoric acid wash. The acid reacts with chlorides and other soluble salts left on the surface and loosens their grip. A high pressure rinse with clean RO water then carries them away, and the pipe is dried.

At your station

Dwell time is set in advance. The rinse uses low conductivity RO water. The whole process is connected to an acid neutralizer and the ETP system, so the waste is treated and not drained. Drying is by compressed-air knife and a 1200 kW induction heater.

Solution: Oakite 31/33

Rinse water: RO, up to 80 °C

Pressure: 150 bar

Flow: 2500 litres/hour

Drying: air knife + 1200 kW induction heater

Waste: acid neutralizer and ETP

The acid wash targets chlorides and soluble salts; the rinse and drying finish the job.

quiz.question: What does the phosphoric acid wash do, according to the deck?
quiz.context: After the blast gate and a first induction pre heat, the pipe meets a phosphoric acid wash. The acid reacts with chlorides and other soluble salts left on the surface and loosens their grip. A high pressure rinse with clean RO water then carries them away, and the pipe is dried.

options.text: Reacts with chlorides and soluble salts so they lose their bond with the pipe surface
options.explanation: The deck says phosphoric acid reacts with chlorides and other soluble salts on the pipe surface so they lose their bond with it. Roughness is the blasting stage’s job, which came earlier.

options.text: Roughens the steel to 50 to 110 µm
options.explanation: The deck says phosphoric acid reacts with chlorides and other soluble salts on the pipe surface so they lose their bond with it. Roughness is the blasting stage’s job, which came earlier.

options.text: Cools the pipe before the epoxy

The clean pipe now passes through two induction heaters in series. They bring it to coating temperature and hold it there. Inline displays show and record the pipe temperature, because the epoxy powder that comes next only behaves correctly on steel at the right heat.

At your station

Watch the temperature display and record. The target is 250 °C, or whatever the FBE powder maker recommends. Two heaters in series are there to keep the surface temperature uniform.

Capacity: 2000 kW

Frequency: 600 to 1500 Hz, variable

Throughput: 125 MT/hr for ΔT 225 °C

Pipe temperature: 250 °C, or per FBE powder

Monitoring: inline display and recording

250 °C is the default. The FBE powder’s own recommendation can override it.

quiz.question: The FBE powder maker recommends a different pipe temperature than 250 °C. What does the deck say?
quiz.context: The clean pipe now passes through two induction heaters in series. They bring it to coating temperature and hold it there. Inline displays show and record the pipe temperature, because the epoxy powder that comes next only behaves correctly on steel at the right heat.

options.text: Hold 250 °C regardless
options.explanation: The deck says the heater helps maintain pipe temperature at 250 °C “or as per recommendation of FBE powder”. The powder data sheet governs.

options.text: Run to the powder maker’s recommendation
options.explanation: The deck says the heater helps maintain pipe temperature at 250 °C “or as per recommendation of FBE powder”. The powder data sheet governs.

options.text: Run cooler to save energy
options.explanation: The deck says the heater helps maintain pipe temperature at 250 °C “or as per recommendation of FBE powder”. The powder data sheet governs.

content.text:
The hot pipe arrives in a spray booth. Up to sixty electrostatic guns coat it with epoxy powder, which melts and fuses on contact with the hot steel. On a 3LPE or 3LPP pipe this is the first of three layers, the primer. On an FBE pipe it is the whole coat, and DFBE uses a second booth for a second layer.

At your station

Powder arrives straight from air-conditioned storage, is sieved and fluidized without a break, and is carried by completely dry, oil-free air. The compressed-air quality is monitored all the time with an alarm. The booth is tied to automatic fire detection and CO₂ suppression.

Spray guns: up to 60 × 20 kg/hr

Spray capacity: 1200 kg/hr

Max thickness, single: 600 µm

Max thickness, dual: 1600 µm

Air dew point: −40 °C

Safety: fire detection + CO₂ suppression

Dry, oil-free air at a −40 °C dew point carries the powder.

quiz.question: The powder is carried by compressed air. What does the deck require of that air?
quiz.context: The hot pipe arrives in a spray booth. Up to sixty electrostatic guns coat it with epoxy powder, which melts and fuses on contact with the hot steel. On a 3LPE or 3LPP pipe this is the first of three layers, the primer. On an FBE pipe it is the whole coat, and DFBE uses a second booth for a second layer.

options.text: Warm and humid
options.explanation: The deck specifies complete dry and oil-free compressed air at a dew point of −40 °C, monitored continuously with an alarm. Moisture or oil in the air reaches the powder and then the coating.

options.text: Completely dry and oil-free, dew point −40 °C
options.explanation: The deck specifies complete dry and oil-free compressed air at a dew point of −40 °C, monitored continuously with an alarm. Moisture or oil in the air reaches the powder and then the coating.

options.text: Any plant air will do
options.explanation: The deck specifies complete dry and oil-free compressed air at a dew point of −40 °C, monitored continuously with an alarm. Moisture or oil in the air reaches the powder and then the coating.

lessons.title: Layers two and three, and the weld seam
lessons.description: ADHESIVE, PE / PP AND SEAM SYSTEM

content.text:
Two extruders feed through flat T-dies: a small one for the adhesive and two large ones for the polyethylene or polypropylene topcoat. A press-on roller smooths the layers onto the pipe. On a spiral pipe, a laser finds the raised weld seam and a plunger pushes extra molten coating over it.

At your station

Dryers take moisture out of the granules before they melt. If the body reads fine but the weld seam reads thin, go to the weld seam system first: laser seam detection and the hydraulic plunger.

Adhesive extruder: 250 kg/hr, 400 mm T-die

PE/PP extruders: 2 × 1200 kg/hr, 1200 mm T-die

Seam detection: laser sensors + PLC

Seam coating: hydraulic plunger over the bead

Application: press-on roller from the top

The weld seam system exists to prevent low thickness on the seam without thickening the whole pipe.

quiz.question: Thickness on the pipe body is fine, but readings right on top of the weld seam are low. Which system do you check first?
quiz.context: Two extruders feed through flat T-dies: a small one for the adhesive and two large ones for the polyethylene or polypropylene topcoat. A press-on roller smooths the layers onto the pipe. On a spiral pipe, a laser finds the raised weld seam and a plunger pushes extra molten coating over it.

options.text: The induction heater
options.explanation: The seam system is built to prevent low coating thickness over the weld seam. The induction heater warms the whole pipe and the quench cools it; neither adds coating to the seam.

options.text: The weld seam system: laser detection and the hydraulic plunger
options.explanation: The seam system is built to prevent low coating thickness over the weld seam. The induction heater warms the whole pipe and the quench cools it; neither adds coating to the seam.

options.text: The quench troughs
options.explanation: The seam system is built to prevent low coating thickness over the weld seam. The induction heater warms the whole pipe and the quench cools it; neither adds coating to the seam.

content.text:
The freshly coated pipe is hot and soft. It slides through a 40 metre zone of controlled water cooling, on the outside and on the inside. The water must flow calmly. A rough pour would leave marks on the new surface.

At your station

Chilled and cooled water are used in different areas. Special troughs keep the flow laminar so there are no water marks. High pressure nozzles cool the inside of the pipe as well.

Length: 40 m

Water: chilled and cooled, by area

Flow: laminar, special troughs

Inside: high pressure nozzles

Laminar flow prevents water marks.

quiz.question: Which statement about the quench matches the deck?
quiz.context: The freshly coated pipe is hot and soft. It slides through a 40 metre zone of controlled water cooling, on the outside and on the inside. The water must flow calmly. A rough pour would leave marks on the new surface.

options.text: Only the outside is cooled
options.explanation: The deck says laminar flow is kept with special troughs to prevent water marks, and the inside is cooled with high pressure nozzles. Chilled and cooled water are used in different areas.

options.text: The outside is cooled with laminar flow troughs and the inside with high pressure nozzles
options.explanation: The deck says laminar flow is kept with special troughs to prevent water marks, and the inside is cooled with high pressure nozzles. Chilled and cooled water are used in different areas.

options.text: Only chilled water is used
options.explanation: The deck says laminar flow is kept with special troughs to prevent water marks, and the inside is cooled with high pressure nozzles. Chilled and cooled water are used in different areas.

lessons.title: Measure it and look at it

content.text:
After quench, the pipe gets its first look and its first measurements. A digital eddy current gauge reads the epoxy layer, the adhesive layer and the total coating thickness. A visual and dimensional inspection follows on the flow chart.

At your station

Calibrate the gauge with standard foils or strips every shift before you trust any reading. Look at the surface and check the dimensions the order calls for.

Gauge: digital eddy current

Measures: epoxy layer, adhesive layer, total thickness

Calibration check: every shift, standard foils/strips

A gauge that was right yesterday is not proven right today. Verify every shift.

quiz.question: It is the start of a new shift. The thickness gauge read perfectly yesterday. Do you use it straight away?
quiz.context: After quench, the pipe gets its first look and its first measurements. A digital eddy current gauge reads the epoxy layer, the adhesive layer and the total coating thickness. A visual and dimensional inspection follows on the flow chart.

options.text: Yes, it was fine yesterday
options.explanation: The deck says calibration is verified with standard calibration foils or strips every shift. A drifting gauge can give readings that look normal.

options.text: No. Verify it against standard foils or strips first
options.explanation: The deck says calibration is verified with standard calibration foils or strips every shift. A drifting gauge can give readings that look normal.

options.text: Only if readings start to look strange
options.explanation: The deck says calibration is verified with standard calibration foils or strips every shift. A drifting gauge can give readings that look normal.

content.text:
A holiday is a pinhole you may not see. An electrode sweeps the coating at high voltage, and wherever there is a hole, current finds the steel. The hooter sounds and the bulb lights. An in-line detector tests the pipe, and portable manual detectors confirm and locate what it finds.

At your station

Ground the pipe and the detector, set the voltage for the coating system, keep the electrode speed at or below the maximum, and calibrate the detector every four hours with jeep meters. Too much voltage can damage the coating.

3LPE / 3LPP voltage: 25 kV, or as specified by client

FBE / DFBE voltage: 5 V per µm (deck: “5 volt/Rm”)

Max electrode speed: 300 mm/s

Detector calibration: every 4 hours, jeep meters

Indication: hooter + indicator bulb

The pass condition is: no holiday, or a holiday that meets the repair criteria and passes the retest.

quiz.question: The in-line test flags a pipe. A manual holiday test confirms one pinhole, and it meets the repair criteria. What next?
quiz.context: A holiday is a pinhole you may not see. An electrode sweeps the coating at high voltage, and wherever there is a hole, current finds the steel. The hooter sounds and the bulb lights. An in-line detector tests the pipe, and portable manual detectors confirm and locate what it finds.

options.text: Reject the pipe
options.explanation: The flow chart sends a holiday that meets the repair criteria to coating repair, then a second manual holiday test. Only OK goes to final inspection. A holiday that does not meet the repair criteria is rejected.

options.text: Repair it, then test again by manual holiday test. If it passes, it goes to final inspection
options.explanation: The flow chart sends a holiday that meets the repair criteria to coating repair, then a second manual holiday test. Only OK goes to final inspection. A holiday that does not meet the repair criteria is rejected.

options.text: Repair it and send it straight to final inspection
options.explanation: The flow chart sends a holiday that meets the repair criteria to coating repair, then a second manual holiday test. Only OK goes to final inspection. A holiday that does not meet the repair criteria is rejected.

content.text:
Some answers cannot be read on a moving line. A strip of coating is pulled straight off the pipe in the lab and the force is measured. It tells you whether the layers are bonded to each other.

At your station

The tester peels at 10 mm per minute, perpendicular to the pipe surface. Results are given as minimum, maximum and average. If a semi-automated machine gives a strange value, suspect the machine before the coating.

Peel rate: 10 mm/min

Direction: perpendicular to the pipe surface

Range: 0 to 2.5 kN

Results: minimum, maximum, average

The peel test measures the bond between top and bottom layers.

quiz.question: A semi-automated peel tester gives one surprisingly low value. Before blaming the coating, what does the deck say to suspect?
quiz.context: Some answers cannot be read on a moving line. A strip of coating is pulled straight off the pipe in the lab and the force is measured. It tells you whether the layers are bonded to each other.

options.text: The pipe end is always weaker
options.explanation: The deck states the semi-automated machine may produce false results because of its inability to adjust to peel angle and speed. That is why the automated tester controls the stripping angle itself.

options.text: The machine: it cannot adjust peel angle and speed, so it may give false results
options.explanation: The deck states the semi-automated machine may produce false results because of its inability to adjust to peel angle and speed. That is why the automated tester controls the stripping angle itself.

options.text: The pipe was tested too soon after quench
options.explanation: The deck states the semi-automated machine may produce false results because of its inability to adjust to peel angle and speed. That is why the automated tester controls the stripping angle itself.

content.text:
After the holiday test the pipe’s ends are cleaned back (cut back cleaning), and it faces final inspection. The inspector checks the coating for defects, measures the cut back and the bevel, and verifies the paperwork. Then the pipe is marked, barcoded, varnished against rust and stacked for dispatch.

At your station

Check as per the ITP: holidays and pinholes, disbonding or delamination, fish eyes and craters, blistering, sagging and drips (3LPE/3LPP), coating damage, surface irregularities, cut back cleaning and length, pipe bevel cleaning, and coating bevel shape.

Defects checked: holidays, disbonding, fish eyes, blistering, sagging

Also checked: coating damage, surface irregularities

Ends: cut back cleaning, length, bevel cleaning, coating bevel shape

Release: marking, barcode, varnish, documents

A pipe leaves only when the coating, the dimensions and the documents all agree.

quiz.question: A pipe passes every physical check, but its documents do not match the coated pipe data. What do you do?
quiz.context: After the holiday test the pipe’s ends are cleaned back (cut back cleaning), and it faces final inspection. The inspector checks the coating for defects, measures the cut back and the bevel, and verifies the paperwork. Then the pipe is marked, barcoded, varnished against rust and stacked for dispatch.

options.text: Release it, the pipe is fine
options.explanation: The deck lists verification of documents with respect to coated pipe data as part of final inspection. A pipe is not cleared until the record and the pipe agree.

options.text: Hold it. Verification of documents against pipe data is part of final inspection
options.explanation: The deck lists verification of documents with respect to coated pipe data as part of final inspection. A pipe is not cleared until the record and the pipe agree.

options.text: Release it and fix the paperwork later
options.explanation: The deck lists verification of documents with respect to coated pipe data as part of final inspection. A pipe is not cleared until the record and the pipe agree.

content.text:
The inside has its own line. Pipes are checked on receipt, preheated in two stations to a dew point condition, blasted in two stations, blown out, and inspected. Failures take the NTC re-process route. The same ideas as outside, with one big difference: moisture control is tied to the dew point of the day.

At your station

Preheating raises the surface temperature to 3 °C above the atmospheric dew point, using whirling hot air inside the pipe. Blasting reaches up to Sa3. The inspection looks at cleanliness, anchor profile, salt or chloride, degree of dust and other defects.

Preheat: 2 parallel stations, hot air

Surface temperature: 3 °C above dew point

Blast sets: 2 parallel, 400 m²/hr each

Cleanliness: up to Sa3

Anchor pattern: 50 to 100 µm

Dust collectors: 2 × 85,000 + 2 × 11,000 CMH

Inside, the surface must be 3 °C above the atmospheric dew point.

quiz.question: Today is humid and the atmospheric dew point is higher than yesterday. What happens to the internal preheat target?
quiz.context: The inside has its own line. Pipes are checked on receipt, preheated in two stations to a dew point condition, blasted in two stations, blown out, and inspected. Failures take the NTC re-process route. The same ideas as outside, with one big difference: moisture control is tied to the dew point of the day.

options.text: Nothing, it is a fixed number
options.explanation: The deck defines the target as a temperature 3 °C above the atmospheric dew point. When the dew point rises, the target rises with it.

options.text: It moves up with the dew point: the surface must be 3 °C above it
options.explanation: The deck defines the target as a temperature 3 °C above the atmospheric dew point. When the dew point rises, the target rises with it.

options.text: The pipe does not need preheating on humid days
options.explanation: The deck defines the target as a temperature 3 °C above the atmospheric dew point. When the dew point rises, the target rises with it.

Tape protects the cut back ends, then a long unsupported lance spins into the pipe as it turns at high speed. A two-part paint is mixed at the lance and sprayed in one smooth, even pass. After the lining, the tape comes off, the pipe is inspected, stencilled, and left to cure in the yard.

At your station

The paint mix ratio is watched by the PLC all the time and held within tolerance. Paint is heated to keep it fluid. The ratio can be set from 1:1 to 10:1 in steps of 0.1, with a ratio check system.

Mixing ratio: 1:1 to 10:1, 0.1 steps

Tolerance: down to ±1%

Thickness range: 50 to 2000 µm

System: plural feed, hot airless

After lining: tape removal, visual inspection, stencilling, curing in yard

The mix ratio is controlled digitally and monitored all the time.

quiz.question: In what order do the cut back tape and the lining go on, according to the internal flow chart?
quiz.context: Tape protects the cut back ends, then a long unsupported lance spins into the pipe as it turns at high speed. A two-part paint is mixed at the lance and sprayed in one smooth, even pass. After the lining, the tape comes off, the pipe is inspected, stencilled, and left to cure in the yard.

options.explanation: The chart shows cut back preparation (tape application), internal coating application, then tape removal, then visual inspection, then stencilling and paint curing at the yard.

options.text: Lining first, then tape

options.text: No tape is used

title: visual inspection
description: Before any machine tests a pipe, a trained eye looks first. In ten stops you learn why, how to set up a proper look, which tools help, and what the common defects look like and why they happen.

content.text:
A pipe that has been cut open to be checked cannot be sold. Non-destructive testing (NDT) examines materials, components or assemblies for discontinuities or differences in characteristics without destroying their usefulness. It is used while a product is made, while it is built into something, and while it is in service.

At your station

NDT is used at almost any stage: to screen incoming material, to monitor and control a process, to verify heat treating or assembly, and to inspect for damage in service. Pick the method that finds the defect or makes the measurement with the best sensitivity and reliability, and weigh the cost.

Also called: NDE, NDI

Used when: incoming material, process control, heat treating, assembly, in-service damage

Main benefit: safer product, less scrap, better reputation

NDT gives an excellent balance between quality control and cost, because the part is still usable afterwards.

Visual testing (VT) is the oldest and most common non-destructive technique, and the first step in examining a casting, forging, machined component or weld. It means examining a material, component or product for non-conformance using light and eyes, alone or with aids.

At your station

VT finds surface flaws: corrosion, contamination, surface finish problems and discontinuities on joints such as welds, seals, solder connections and adhesive bonds. It is easy to use throughout a job, so simple errors are caught before they spread. A trained inspector also shakes, listens, feels and sometimes smells.

Finds: cracks, corrosion, contamination, finish, surface discontinuities

Strength: cheapest and widest-used, first step

Needs: a trained eye, light, access

VT needs no equipment except the naked eye of a trained inspector, but it still needs a trained inspector.

quiz.question: Why do inspectors still do visual testing even when another NDT method is also used?

options.explanation: The deck calls VT the first step in the examination process, and says that even when other techniques detect surface cracks, visual inspection often gives a useful supplement. It does not find internal flaws.

options.text: It is the first step and often supplements other methods in finding surface cracks

A clean, comfortable, well-lit place with reasonable access. A test piece free of coatings, oil and grease. Calibrated equipment the inspector understands. And the eye at the right distance and angle, under enough light to resolve a very fine line.

At your station

Clean the surface. Check the light. Keep your eye within 600 mm of the surface at an angle of at least 30° (ASME Sec V, Art. 9). Use a magnifier if required. The test is judged adequate if you can resolve a 0.8 mm wide black line on an artificial flaw on the surface.

Eye distance: within 600 mm

Viewing angle: 30° or more

Light (ASME V Art. 9): 350 lux min, over 500 recommended

Light (API 5L, 45th ed.): 300 lux min

Light (ASME V / API 5LD): 1000 lux min

Resolve: a 0.8 mm black line

Near vision: Jaeger No. 2 at ≥12 in, annual

Colour vision: every 5 years

Different standards ask for different light. Your contract decides which number applies.

lessons.title: The method and three ways to look

content.text:
A visual inspection has three steps: clean the surface, light it properly, examine it. And there are three ways to look: with the eye alone, with the eye plus an aid, or through a camera.

At your station

Clean off oil, grease, scale and sand, because contaminants can mislead you. Light the specimen well: the human eye is most sensitive to yellow-green light (wavelength 5560 Å). Then examine with the eyes, or with light-sensitive devices such as photocells.

Step 1: clean the inspection surface

Step 2: light it adequately

Step 3: examine with eyes or light-sensitive devices

Best eye sensitivity: yellow-green, 5560 Å

Direct aided keeps the image the same, only bigger or filtered. Remote turns it into an electronic image.

lessons.title: Light, surfaces and the inspector’s aids

content.text:
Lighting is of extreme importance. How a surface reflects light, what shape it has, and what colour it is all decide how well you can see a defect. The inspector’s kit then adds mirrors, magnifiers, borescopes, video probes, robots and gauges.

At your station

Pick the lighting to suit the surface. Specular surfaces are mirror-like. Diffuse surfaces scatter light and look dull. Directional surfaces carry fine grooves. Use coloured or selective filters to improve contrast between a defect and its background.

Mirrors: look inside pipes, threaded holes, hard-to-see places

Magnifiers: surface finish, profile, microstructure

Borescopes: rigid or flexible, closed or inaccessible areas

Video probes and robots: tanks, ducts, pipelines, hazardous spaces

Weld gauges: fillet, height, undercut depth, misalignment

Choose the light for the surface. The same defect can be invisible under one light and obvious under another.

Seeing is not enough. Defects have sizes, and sizes have limits. The inspector’s toolbox runs from thin steel rules to clock gauges that read to a thousandth of a millimetre.

At your station

Use thin steel rules to reduce parallax error and keep stability. Use tapes for longer distances, checked at a specified temperature and tension. Use vernier calipers, micrometers and clock gauges when you need finer readings.

Steel rule: 0.5 mm or 1/64 in

Tape rule: 1 mm, 1 m to 100 m

Vernier caliper: 0.01 mm or 0.005 in

Micrometer: 0.001 mm or 0.0005 in

Clock gauge: 0.001 mm or 0.00005 in

Pick the instrument whose smallest reading is finer than the tolerance you are checking.

Before a pipe is a pipe, it is steel plate from a mill. The deck lists eleven defects found on steel: sliver, scab, rolled-in scale, roll mark, tong mark, dents or indentation marks, pitting, seam line, lap, lamination and hair line cracks. Plus shell, roll-in bolt and roll-in wire.

At your station

Match the look to the description. Slivers come from tearing of corners during rolling. Scabs are irregular patches of metal. Rolled-in scale is old scale pressed into the surface. Seam lines are long, shallow grooves. Hair line cracks are internal and need etching or magnetic crack detection to see.

Sliver: tearing of corners during rolling

Scab: irregular patch from mould cavities or loose layers

Rolled-in scale: old scale pressed in during rolling

Seam line: long shallow grooves

Shell: thin film imperfectly attached

Hair cracks: internal, seen by etching or magnetic crack detection

Learn each defect with its origin. The picture and the cause confirm each other.

A good plate can still become a poor pipe. The deck lists six defects found on the body of a finished pipe: improper grinding, deep grinding, roller mark, chip mark, scratches and mechanical damage, including chisel marks.

At your station

Use the photos to build your eye. The deck shows each defect as a labelled photograph. Note the position, the length and the shape, because the limits you apply will depend on them.

Defects listed: improper grinding, deep grinding, roller mark, chip mark, scratches, mechanical damage

Shown in deck: photographs with scales

Not in deck: causes and acceptance limits

These defects are usually made by handling or finishing, so they can often be prevented.

content.text:
The deck lists twenty weld defects, from poor toe blend to distortion. For each, it shows the look and the causes. The good inspector reads the defect backwards to its cause, because that is how a welder fixes it.

At your station

Start with the features of a good butt weld: cap width, excess weld metal height, root penetration and root bead width, plus profile, toe blend and weld width. Then learn the common defects: root defects, undercut, lack of fusion, porosity, slag, burn-through, spatter, arc strikes, cracks and distortion.

Total defects listed: 20

Root family: incomplete penetration, incomplete fusion, concavity, excess penetration, undercut

Fusion family: lack of fusion, lack of side wall and inter-run fusion

Inclusions: slag, tungsten

Others: burn through, spatter, arc strikes, cracks, distortion

The defect tells you what happened. The cause list tells you what to change.

lessons.title: Where the eye matters on the coating line

content.text:
You now know how to look. On the coating line, trained eyes are used at the blast gate, after the quench and at final inspection. The same discipline applies: clean, light, look, measure.

At your station

At the blast gate: visual cleanliness against ISO 8501-1 and SSPC-VIS 1, with a roughness gauge and a salt meter. After quench: visual and dimensional inspection, with a thickness gauge verified every shift. At final inspection: coating defects, cut back and bevel checks and document verification.

Blast gate: visual grade, roughness, salt, dust

After quench: visual, dimensional, thickness

Final inspection: coating defects, cut back, bevel, documents

Good inspection habits travel. Light, angle, distance, tools, method.
